name: VDB
description: VDB returns depreciation for any interval, including partial periods, and can switch to straight-line depreciation when beneficial.
tldr: Calculates variable declining balance depreciation for any period you specify.

parameters.name: salvage
parameters.description: Value at the end of the depreciation life.

parameters.name: life
parameters.description: Number of periods over which the asset is depreciated.

parameters.name: start_period
parameters.description: Starting period for which to calculate depreciation.

parameters.name: end_period
parameters.description: Ending period for which to calculate depreciation.

parameters.name: no_switch
parameters.description: If TRUE, does not switch to straight-line (default FALSE).

basicExample.description: Depreciation for the first year using declining balance with straight-line switch
basicExample.explanation: First-year depreciation for a $10,000 asset using double-declining balance, switching to straight-line if beneficial.

advancedExamples.title: Cumulative depreciation for years 2-4
advancedExamples.description: Total depreciation from the start of year 2 to the end of year 4
advancedExamples.explanation: VDB can calculate depreciation over a range of periods.

howItWorks: VDB combines the declining balance method with an optional straight-line switch. By default, it switches to straight-line when that gives higher depreciation. This maximizes the deduction while ensuring the asset is not depreciated below salvage value.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Can calculate depreciation for a single period or a range of periods.
Automatically switches to straight-line unless no_switch is TRUE.
More flexible than DDB for partial periods and range calculations.

commonErrors.cause: Start or end period is invalid or cost < salvage.
commonErrors.fix: Check period values and ensure cost >= salvage.
Use the default or FALSE for no_switch to allow straight-line switch.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: VDB works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between VDB and DDB?
faq.answer: VDB can switch to straight-line and can calculate depreciation over a range. DDB uses pure declining balance.

faq.question: When should I use VDB?
faq.answer: Use VDB when you want the most tax-efficient depreciation method that combines declining balance and straight-line.
